Photograph: Jeff Greenberg/Universal Images Group/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Budget airline Jetstar is changing its carry-on baggage allowance rules to charge fees for using the overhead locker. Photograph: Jeff Greenberg/Universal Images Group/Getty Images Jetstar Jetstar to charge fees up to $52 to put carry-on baggage in overhead lockers Airline says struggling to find room in overhead lockers on planes a ‘stressful part of the airport experience’ Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Guardian staff Tue 4 Aug 2026 18.54 EDT First published on Tue 4 Aug 2026 17.42 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Jetstar will charge its passengers up to $52 to put carry-on baggage in the overhead locker, in a major change to the budget airline’s carry-on rules. In a press release on Wednesday morning, the airline announced it would remove the 7kg weight limit for carry-on bags, beginning in February 2027. There will still be size restrictions. The change to baggage allowance follows extensive research and feedback from customers and crew who consistently identified having bags weighed at the gate and struggling to find room in overhead lockers as the more stressful parts of the airport experience, the airline said. So how do you get access to the Qantas chairman’s lounge? Alan Joyce has some tips Read more “We know that weighing carry-on bags at the gate can be frustrating for our customers and for our crew,” the CEO of Jetstar, Stephanie Tully, said. Instead, all bookings will include one underseat bag such as a backpack, handbag or laptop bag. Customers who need more carry-on baggage can pay a “Priority Carry-on” fee, which includes a second, larger bag for the overhead locker and the opportunity to be among the first to board. Prices depend on the flight: $25 for Launceston to Sydney, $33 Sydney to Melbourne, and up to $52 for Cairns to Tokyo. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email The size-based carry-on baggage model is “similar to other leading low-fares carriers around the world”, the airline said. “From February, the main thing customers will need to think about is the size of their carry-on,” Tully said. “By giving customers an underseat bag with the option to add Priority Carry-on, we can make better use of overhead locker space, streamline boarding and help more flights depart on time. “Our new carry-on baggage model provides more choice to customers while helping to keep our fares low. You only pay for what you need – travelling with less means paying less, and you can always add more if you need.” skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks Preview latest after newsletter promotion Jetstar will no longer routinely use cabin baggage scales but will still ask customers to keep carry-on bags to 10kg so they can safely lift it themselves. Customers travelling with an infant will be able to take an extra underseat bag for their baby items, at no extra cost. The underseat bags can be up to 40 × 30 × 20cm and overhead bags can be up to 56 × 36 × 23cm. There are no changes to Jetstar’s checked baggage allowance, which remains purchasable for up to 40kg per passenger. in defense news Hensoldt introduces KENIS sensor and secures major customer order at AAD 2026 Share Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Email WhatsApp Hensoldt South Africa has marked the launch of its KENIS 1280 AK thermal imaging sensor as a standalone product with a significant customer agreement signed during the Africa Aerospace and Defence (AAD) 2026 exhibition in Pretoria last week. Hensoldt South Africa and Estonia-based HEVI Optronics signed an agreement for the supply of 200 KENIS 1280 AK sensors, which will be integrated into HEVI’s systems for long-range surveillance and Counter-Unmanned Aerial System (C-UAS) applications. The agreement builds on HEVI’s previous procurement of 150 KENIS sensors and further strengthens the cooperation between the two companies. The agreement represents an important milestone for Hensoldt South Africa as it expands the availability of the KENIS technology beyond its own optronic systems and into the wider market for high-performance sensor solutions, the company said. “The KENIS 1280 AK has been proven in our own systems for more than five years. Making it available as a standalone sensor is a natural next step, and securing an order of this scale at AAD is a strong validation of the market opportunity,” said Sunette Van Rensburg, Head of Sales, Optronics at Hensoldt South Africa. The KENIS 1280 AK is a cooled mid-wave infrared (MWIR) thermal imaging sensor designed for long-range surveillance, target identification and C-UAS applications. It has already been deployed as a core sensor in Hensoldt’s flagship ARGOS-15 and BushBaby 200 systems for more than five years. The strategy to offer the sensor as a standalone product reflects growing demand from system integrators seeking proven, high-performance thermal imaging technology that can be incorporated into their own solutions, Hensoldt South Africa said. The sensor is designed for integration into a broad range of applications, including stabilised airborne systems, land and naval surveillance, border and coastal security, situational awareness and C-UAS solutions. Its compact size, weight and power requirements also support integration into systems where space and available power are constrained. At the heart of the KENIS 1280 AK is a high-resolution 1280 × 1024 MWIR detector, combined with a 30× continuous optical zoom and Hensoldt South Africa’s proprietary video-processing technology. Together, these capabilities provide operators and automated systems with detailed thermal imagery for detecting, tracking and identifying targets at long range. For HEVI Optronics, the KENIS 1280 AK forms part of its approach to delivering high-fidelity sensing capabilities for its HeviTrack-M platforms. “HEVI Optronics has standardised the integration of the KENIS 1280 sensor suite from Hensoldt South Africa to meet the growing demand for high-resolution thermal imaging in long-range detection and C-UAS applications,” said Kristjan Tiimus, Chief Executive Officer of HEVI Optronics. The KENIS 1280 AK is the first sensor from this portfolio that Hensoldt South Africa is making available as a standalone product. Its established use within Hensoldt systems provides system integrators with access to technology that has already been fielded and matured in demanding operational environments, the company said. “The agreement with HEVI Optronics demonstrates the potential of this approach and opens further opportunities for Hensoldt South Africa to support customers developing the next generation of electro-optical and multi-sensor systems,” Hensoldt South Africa said. The company offers a comprehensive range of products, systems and services across defence and civil markets, from electronic warfare and optronics, spectrum monitoring and security solutions, to radar, IFF and datalinks. With more than 700 South African employees across five sites in South Africa, it is the Hensoldt Group’s largest industrial base outside of Europe and one of the largest defence and security electronics companies in South Africa.
